network.tdh.verify.metadataDescription: Every day, the Rust core that validators will run, the Python reference and 6529.io’s TDH side by side: how many identity records agree, and every difference counted and classed by cause.

network.tdh.verify.title: TDH verification
network.tdh.verify.lede: Every day, the Rust core that validators will run and the Python reference compute every collector’s TDH, and both are compared with 6529.io’s published values. Differences are counted and classed by cause; no individual record is published.

network.tdh.verify.mode.unchecked: History read from Ethereum log servers, not yet fully checked. The snapshot block is linked header by header to a recent finalized block, and the edition floors are proven against it; that finalized block is taken from a public beacon server once others confirm it, with no pinned checkpoint yet. The history before the snapshot was read from public log servers and is taken as reported. This label changes when 6529’s own Ethereum node, expected about October 18, is synced and the full check runs against it. Nothing in these runs signs.

network.tdh.verify.side.heading: Side by side
network.tdh.verify.side.caption: The day’s results from each implementation. 6529.io’s values are the object under test.
network.tdh.verify.side.runtimeNote: Rust’s includes reading Ethereum and checking what is checked today: the day’s headers, linked to a finalized block, and the proofs of the edition floors. The history before the snapshot is not yet checked. Computing a day takes it about 0.6 s
network.tdh.verify.side.rootsHelp: The cycle root binds the day, the snapshot block, the rule version with its registry hash, every wallet record outside the two sinks, each identity’s TDH per card, and the counts and total; validators will sign it. Equal record files give equal roots.
network.tdh.verify.side.pythonRoots: None: its record files are compared byte for byte with Rust’s
network.tdh.verify.side.computedPython: Computed from the Rust run’s input, SHA-256 checked
network.tdh.verify.diff.heading: Differences
network.tdh.verify.diff.lede: A difference is any identity or wallet record that is not equal in every compared field, between the Rust core and the Python reference or between the Rust core and 6529.io. Each is counted once, with its class and its cause.
network.tdh.verify.diff.none: No differences: every identity and wallet record is equal in every compared field, between the Rust core and 6529.io and between the Rust core and the Python reference.
network.tdh.verify.diff.countsMissing: Records differ on this day, but its file carries no counts by class.
network.tdh.verify.diff.privacy: Individual records are never published, not even under a label: one differing token can single out its holder. The daily job keeps the per-record detail in a private report and publishes only these counts.
network.tdh.verify.diff.history: How it started: before transaction netting, the runs of October 14 and 15 had 10,280 of 10,282 identity records and 11,131 of 11,133 wallet records equal, with totals 240 TDH below 6529.io’s. Both differences were DEV-2 cases, each a token sent out and back within one transaction. D131’s netting settled them, and the reruns of those two days are equal everywhere.
network.tdh.verify.class.A.body: Against 6529.io: a known, deliberate difference between TDH-v1 and the old backend (a DEV item).
network.tdh.verify.class.B.body: Against 6529.io: a known issue in the old backend (a BUG item).
network.tdh.verify.class.C.body: The Rust core and the Python reference disagree: a defect in the new software.
network.tdh.verify.class.D.body: Against 6529.io, with no known cause. Every difference is class D until it is matched to a known one, and it raises an alarm.
network.tdh.verify.class.note: Class A and B differences are explained, not accepted: the owner still decides what to do with each. Since D131’s netting the list of known differences is empty, so any difference from 6529.io raises an alarm.

network.tdh.verify.provenance.heading: Provenance
network.tdh.verify.provenance.remote: 6529’s public TDH feed, served from 6529’s CloudFront address d379duzqnomz3w.cloudfront.net: the daily job’s published files, linked below. It publishes once a day after its 00:40 UTC run, and fetches a late 6529.io file again at 06:00 and 12:00 UTC; this page rechecks the files every 10 minutes. The files are not signed: the SHA-256 below is the page’s own reading of them.
network.tdh.verify.provenance.ruleFromSp: TDH-v1, rule version tdh-v1.0. This day’s file does not state its rule version; this is the specification’s.
network.tdh.verify.provenance.registryFr: The specification’s hash for tdh-v1.0; not stated in this day’s file.
network.tdh.verify.provenance.commitsNot: Neither repository is public: the validator’s is to be published when the owner decides (D116), and the Python reference is in 6529’s private design repository. Each run records its commits, so it can be reproduced from them.
network.tdh.verify.provenance.txLink: Open the Arweave transaction {id}: its signer, size and data root
network.tdh.verify.provenance.signed: The comparison accepts a file only when 6529.io’s upload key signed it and its size and data root are the signed ones.
network.tdh.verify.check.heading: Check it yourself
network.tdh.verify.check.intro: What anyone can check today, what that does not reach, and how a day is reproduced with the source code.
network.tdh.verify.check.upload: 6529.io’s own public API lists every day’s upload with its block and a link to its file on Arweave. Open the day’s file from that list and check on Arweave that its signer is 6529.io’s upload key:
network.tdh.verify.check.block: Open the snapshot block on a block explorer: it is the last block before 00:00 UTC of the day.
network.tdh.verify.check.file: Download the day’s JSON above: every number on this page comes from it.
network.tdh.verify.check.limit: None of this reaches the Rust or Python numbers: checking them needs their source code, which is not public. The validator’s, with the Rust core and the daily tools, is to be published when the owner decides (D116); the Python reference is in 6529’s private design repository.
network.tdh.verify.check.sourceBody: A day’s run is three commands, from the validator repository with a checkout of 6529’s design repository beside it, which holds the Python reference. The Rust run reads Ethereum and writes its canonical input; the Python reference computes from that input after checking its SHA-256; the three-way comparison fetches 6529.io’s files, verifies them and compares every record:
network.tdh.verify.check.compare: Then compare: your cycle root and wallet root must equal the ones on this page, and your identities.jsonl and wallets.jsonl must equal your own Python run’s byte for byte.
network.tdh.verify.method.heading: How this works
network.tdh.verify.method.snapshot.title: The same snapshot.
network.tdh.verify.method.snapshot.body: All three use the snapshot block of the day, the last Ethereum block before 00:00 UTC.
network.tdh.verify.method.inputs.title: Independent computation.
network.tdh.verify.method.inputs.body: The Rust core reads the day’s events from Ethereum and computes TDH-v1. The Python reference computes from the same input, after checking its SHA-256, so the two compare computation, not reading Ethereum. 6529.io’s values come from the files it publishes every day on Arweave, accepted only when the upload key’s signature and the file’s size and data root verify. 6529.io’s values are the object under test, never an input.
network.tdh.verify.method.exact.title: Exact comparison.
network.tdh.verify.method.exact.body: The TDH fields of every collector and wallet are compared for exact equality, with no tolerance: each record’s boost, boosted TDH, TDH and unweighted days; the same three TDH values for each collection; and for every token its balance, rate, TDH and unweighted days. Record counts, totals and the snapshot block are compared too. The upload’s other columns (ranks, balance and set counts, BUG-15, and display names) are not written by these runs and are not compared.
network.tdh.verify.method.classes.title: Classification.
network.tdh.verify.method.classes.body: Each differing record is classed A to D. Only differences on the list of known ones are explained; any other is class D and raises an alarm.
network.tdh.verify.method.after.title: After the cutover,
network.tdh.verify.method.after.body: 6529.io runs the Rust core, so their agreement shows that what is published is what was computed. The Python reference stays the independent check of the computation.
network.tdh.verify.method.validators: Once validators run, P53 requires each to sign before it reads 6529.io’s values, so those values cannot influence its vote.
network.tdh.verify.flow.title: The daily comparison
network.tdh.verify.flow.desc: Two flows meet in the comparison. Ethereum feeds the Rust core, and the Python reference computes from the Rust run’s input. Separately, 6529.io’s backend publishes its upload on Arweave. The comparison publishes the files this page reads.
network.tdh.verify.flow.sameCode: After the cutover, the 6529.io backend runs the same Rust core.
network.tdh.verify.flow.text: Ethereum → Rust core. The Rust run’s input, SHA-256 checked → Python reference. Both → Compare. 6529.io backend → Arweave upload → Compare. Compare → published JSON → this page. After the cutover, the 6529.io backend runs the Rust core.

network.tdh.verify.provenance.p26Run: These runs followed P26 at {commit}, the Python reference’s commit in this day’s file. That text has the same rule version and registry hash as P26’s latest: tdh-v1.0 is not frozen until launch, so the commit names the text.
network.tdh.verify.provenance.daySha: SHA-256 of this day’s file, as this page read it:
network.tdh.verify.class.expected: Expected until the owner decides: a group of four consolidated wallets, which 6529.io accepts for links registered from its start date. 6529.io groups all four; the Rust core and the Python reference group three, as P26 §6.3 requires. Such a group would show here as class D, not yet explained, and raise an alarm.
network.tdh.verify.check.uploadSum: the key behind every upload the API lists. Then add up the file’s boosted TDH column: you get the 6529.io total on this page.
network.tdh.verify.class.expectedDev2: Expected until the cutover: a sale and a purchase of one card in different transactions of one block. TDH-v1 keeps their on-chain order (DEV-2) and the old backend does not, so a few wallets’ TDH can differ; D132 names it as the one difference that remains until the cutover. It is not on the list of known differences, so it would show here as class D, not yet explained, and raise an alarm until it is matched. It ends when 6529.io switches to the Rust core.
